message.content:
Worker in a git worktree of the Fortress revival repo. Orientation: CLAUDE.md (build/run section — env setup, ant compileAll once in your worktree, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD, unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS); explorations/microgpt-port.md (the v1 port's methodology and verified numbers); explorations/microgpt.fss (the v1 program itself — note its gauss() Box–Muller over the library's random(), the nano config in run(), and that the deterministic init formula appears only in goldenCheck).

Question from Pavol (the project owner): our golden verification deliberately eliminated PRNG differences via a deterministic weight formula, because Fortress lacks Python's Mersenne Twister. What happens when each side uses its own native PRNG — Fortress the standard library's random(), Python its stock random module? Do the two implementations still land in the same training regime, or does the PRNG choice visibly matter?

Tasks:
1. Characterize Fortress's native PRNG as implemented in this tree: find the interpreter glue for random() (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/ is the likely home), identify the underlying generator (java.util.Random? seeded how?), whether it can be seeded from Fortress source, and whether runs are reproducible across JVM invocations. Cite file:line.
2. Re-assemble Karpathy's microgpt.py from karpathy.github.io/2026/02/12/microgpt/ into the scratchpad (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/) — do NOT put it anywhere in the repo, its license is unstated. Adapt it to the v1 nano config (read microgpt-port.md for: n_embd 8, 2 heads, block 8, 2000 docs of explorations/names.txt, 250 steps, and the same Adam/LR constants as microgpt.fss) but with Karpathy's own stock-random initialization (his original init and sampling, Mersenne Twister). Run it with ~5 different seeds; record the loss trajectories (per-10-step values) and final samples.
3. Run the v1 Fortress program as-is (its training already uses native random()): ./bin/fortress explorations/microgpt.fss with env FORTRESS_THREADS=1, generous timeout (30+ min; it prints loss every 10 steps and samples at the end). Run it twice if the PRNG turns out to be time-seeded (to see run-to-run spread), once if it is fixed-seeded (then explain what determinism that implies). NOTE: goldenCheck runs first and must still PASS — it is PRNG-independent.
4. Compare: do the Fortress trajectory and the Python trajectories share the same band (v1 reference: ~3.29 falling to ~2.3 by step 250)? Are final losses within the cross-seed spread of the Python runs? Are samples comparably name-like? Any qualitative divergence attributable to the PRNG (e.g. gauss tail behavior, Box–Muller vs Python's gauss)?

Caveats: two other workers are running on this machine, so treat wall-clock timings as indicative only; loss values are unaffected. Do not commit or push; do not modify tracked files.

Deliverable: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/prng-report.md — the PRNG characterization with citations, the trajectory table (Fortress run(s) vs Python seeds), and a verdict paragraph answering Pavol's question. Final message: compact summary + report path.

67	linear(x: Array[\V,ZZ32\], m: Mat): Array[\V,ZZ32\] =
68	  array[\V\](m.rows).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => do
69	    var acc: V := konst(0.0)

73	softmaxA(x: Array[\V,ZZ32\], n: ZZ32): Array[\V,ZZ32\] = do
74	  var mx: RR64 := x[0].data
75	  for i <- seq(1#(n - 1)) do if x[i].data > mx then mx := x[i].data end end
76	  exps = array[\V\](n).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => (x[i] - konst(mx)).expV())
77	  var tot: V := konst(0.0)
78	  for i <- seq(0#n) do tot := tot + exps[i] end
79	  inv = tot.pow(-1.0)

83	rmsnorm(x: Array[\V,ZZ32\], n: ZZ32): Array[\V,ZZ32\] = do
84	  var ms: V := konst(0.0)
85	  for i <- seq(0#n) do ms := ms + (x[i] DOT x[i]) end
86	  ms := ms DOT konst(1.0 / (n 1.0))
87	  scale = (ms + konst(0.00001)).pow(-0.5)

1	# microgpt.fss — feasibility map (2026-08-23)
2	
3	Status: **idea on the goals list; mapping only, no code yet.** Decided
4	with Pavol in the post-C2 goals discussion.
5	
6	Target: Karpathy's **microgpt** (published 2026-02-12,
7	karpathy.github.io/2026/02/12/microgpt/) — a complete GPT in 243 lines
8	of dependency-free Python: scalar reverse-mode autodiff (`Value`),
9	char-level tokenizer, a 1-layer/4-head transformer (rmsnorm, attention
10	with KV cache, relu MLP), Adam with bias correction and linear LR decay,
11	temperature sampling. Trains on makemore's `names.txt` and hallucinates
12	new names. Source recovered from the blog post (scratchpad copy);
13	`docs`/`Tokenizer`/`Value`/`gpt`/`Adam`/inference sections all in hand.
14	
15	Why this target: it is the *scalar-autodiff* formulation — no tensors,
16	no numpy — so it exercises exactly what Fortress is good at (objects,
17	operator overloading, mathematical notation) and nothing we lack. The
18	Fortress version becomes the mathematical-notation twin: the same
19	program, but the forward/backward math typesets via Fortify.
20	
21	Model size at Karpathy's defaults: vocab ≈ 28, n_embd 16, block 16,
22	1 layer ⇒ ≈ 4,200 parameters; ~10⁵ graph nodes per training step,
23	1,000 steps ⇒ order 10⁸ scalar graph operations for the full run.
24	
25	## What it needs → what the 2012 library has
26	
27	Language features — **all present**:
28	
29	| microgpt needs | Fortress |
30	|---|---|
31	| class with mutable fields (`Value.data/.grad`) | `object` with `var` fields |
32	| operator overloading on own type (`+ * / ** neg`) | `opr` methods — core strength |
33	| closures, local recursive fn (`build_topo`) | `fn` lambdas, local functions |
34	| list comprehensions, `zip`, slicing `q[a:b]` | comprehensions `<\|...\|>`, `List.zip`, range indexing `a[lo#len]` |
35	| sequential loops (training is stateful) | `for i <- seq(...)` — parallel-by-default needs explicit `seq` |
36	
37	Library — **present and interpreter-tested**:
38	
39	| microgpt needs | Library has |
40	|---|---|
41	| growable list (`append`, `reversed`) | `List` (addRight, reverse, zip, indexOf); arrays for the buffers |
42	| dict `state_dict` | `Map` exists — but named fields in a model object are better Fortress anyway |
43	| `random.shuffle` | `Shuffle.shuffle` (list + array variants, fairness-documented) |
44	| uniform random | `random(a):RR64`, `randomZZ32` natives (buffons uses them) |
45	| `math.log/exp`, `** 0.5` | `RR64.log/exp`, `^` on RR64 (realArith-tested) |
46	| read `input.txt` lines | `FileReadStream.lines()` (FileSupport; FileReadWrite tests) |
47	| chars of a string, `uchars.index(ch)` | String is a generator of `Char`; `indexOf` |
48	| `print(f"...")` | `println`; `Format` library for the fancy bits |

50	## Gaps — all small, all writable in .fss
51	
52	1. **No gaussian sampler** (`random.gauss`) → Box–Muller from
53	   `random()`, ~4 lines.
54	2. **No weighted sampling** (`random.choices`) → CDF scan over the
55	   probs, ~5 lines.
56	3. **Identity-based visited set** in `backward()`'s topo sort — Python
57	   uses object-identity hashing. Fortress has `opr SEQV(a:Any,b:Any)`
58	   (object equivalence) but no identity-hashed Set. Cleaner adaptation:
59	   a `var visited:Boolean` flag on the node (or an epoch counter),
60	   reset per backward pass. Design note, not a blocker.
61	4. **`names.txt` download** — the Python fetches it at first run; we
62	   commit-or-fetch it separately (32k one-word lines, public domain
63	   names corpus from makemore).
64	5. **Verify, not assumed:** a list/array `sort` for the unique-chars
65	   vocabulary (worst case: 30-element insertion sort inline), and
66	   `Format` for `%.4f`-style loss printing.

68	## Types — the direct answer
69	
70	The port needs `RR64` scalars, `ZZ32` indices, `String`/`Char`,
71	`Boolean`, and one user object type. All exist; the numeric tower and
72	ZZ32→RR64 coercions are exercised by the whole test suite. No tensors
73	are involved anywhere — that's the point of the scalar formulation —
74	so the known library gaps (no ℂ, no linear algebra, incomplete/
75	directory) do not touch this project. The typed-tensor/shape-checking
76	showcase is a *separate, later* étude on top of Fortress's
77	dimension-typed arrays; microgpt needs none of it.
78	
79	## Risks and de-risking (v2 — after adversarial pass, 2026-08-23)
80	
81	Correctness:
82	
83	- **Floating-point association is the top correctness trap.** Python's
84	  `sum()` is a sequential left fold; Fortress Σ/BIG operators reduce as
85	  trees and its loops are parallel by default — different summation
86	  order means different rounding, spuriously failing goldens and
87	  nondeterministic runs. Rule: **the reference port is sequential
88	  everywhere** (seq loops, left folds); an idiomatic-parallel variant
89	  is a separate later artifact. Port audit item: every loop,
90	  comprehension, and reduction justified as pure-or-seq.
91	- **Transcendental ulp drift**: Java's Math.pow/exp/log and CPython's
92	  libm can differ in the last ulp, and error compounds over ~10⁴-node
93	  graphs. Golden tolerances: relative ~1e-9 forward, ~1e-6 gradients;
94	  and goldens run on *short* inputs (1-position and 3-position
95	  sequences) where accumulation is small — full docs are covered by
96	  the statistical band, not goldens.
97	- **Golden weights carry no RNG**: both harnesses fill weights from the
98	  same deterministic formula, e.g. w[i][j] = ((31 i + 17 j) mod 97
99	  − 48)/100. Documented once, implemented twice.
100	- **Boundary/literal details to pin in stage 1**: relu gradient at
101	  exactly 0 is 0 (match Python's `float(data > 0)`); verify RR64
102	  scientific-notation literals (`1.0e-8`) early — fall back to written-
103	  out decimals if the parser objects.
104	
105	Performance:
106	
107	- **Interpreter throughput** is the dominant unknown. Revised workload:
108	  average name ≈ 7 tokens ⇒ ~40–50k graph nodes per step, ~4×10⁷
109	  node-ops for the full run, plus interpreter constant factors. The
110	  step-0 benchmark separates the costs instead of one blended number:
111	  (a) raw scalar-arithmetic ceiling, (b) object allocation + `opr`
112	  dispatch (build a Value chain), (c) forward+backward over a
113	  micro-graph, (d) Array vs. List dot product — the library List is a
114	  finger tree with O(log n) indexing, so hot buffers likely want
115	  arrays.
116	- **Memory**: interpreter values are heavyweight; 40–50k live nodes per
117	  step could mean hundreds of MB. The benchmark records RSS; heap flags
118	  via the bin/fortress JAVA_FLAGS defaults if needed.
119	- **Node-fusion lever** (if the raw port is too slow): a `dot(xs, ws)`
120	  operation as a *single* Value node with per-child local gradients —
121	  microgpt's Value already carries n-ary children/local-grads, Karpathy
122	  just never added the op. Cuts node count ~16×, mathematically
123	  identical. Held in reserve, not the first move.
124	- **Fallback config**: a nano setting (n_embd 8, block 8, ~200 steps,
125	  doc subset) sized from the measured ops/sec so a full training run
126	  lands under ~30 minutes even in the slow case.
127	- **Recursion depth**: `build_topo` recurses to graph depth (longest
128	  chain, hundreds) — fine; `-Xss` or a work-list version if the Java
129	  stack ever objects.
130	
131	CPython reference bar (measured above): 120 s. The port target is
132	"within an order of magnitude"; the levers above are the path there.

# Let there be a Tokenizer to translate strings to discrete symbols and back

n_embd = 16     # embedding dimension
n_head = 4      # number of attention heads
n_layer = 1     # number of layers
block_size = 16 # maximum sequence length
head_dim = n_embd // n_head # dimension of each head
matrix = lambda nout, nin, std=0.08: [[Value(random.gauss(0, std)) for _ in range(nin)] for _ in range(nout)]
state_dict = {'wte': matrix(vocab_size, n_embd), 'wpe': matrix(block_size, n_embd), 'lm_head': matrix(vocab_size, n_embd)}
for i in range(n_layer):

    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wk'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wv'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wo'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.mlp_fc1'] = matrix(4 * n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.mlp_fc2'] = matrix(n_embd, 4 * n_embd)

def linear(x, w):
    return [sum(wi * xi for wi, xi in zip(wo, x)) for wo in w]

=========== BLOCK 9 ===========
def softmax(logits):
    max_val = max(val.data for val in logits)
    exps = [(val - max_val).exp() for val in logits]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [e / total for e in exps]

def rmsnorm(x):
    ms = sum(xi * xi for xi in x) / len(x)
    scale = (ms + 1e-5) ** -0.5
    return [xi * scale for xi in x]

def gpt(token_id, pos_id, keys, values):
    tok_emb = state_dict['wte'][token_id] # token embedding
    pos_emb = state_dict['wpe'][pos_id] # position embedding
    x = [t + p for t, p in zip(tok_emb, pos_emb)] # joint token and position embedding
    x = rmsnorm(x)

    for li in range(n_layer):
        # 1) Multi-head attention block
        x_residual = x
        x = rmsnorm(x)
        q = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wq'])
        k = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wk'])
        v = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wv'])
        keys[li].append(k)
        values[li].append(v)
        x_attn = []
        for h in range(n_head):
            hs = h * head_dim
            q_h = q[hs:hs+head_dim]
            k_h = [ki[hs:hs+head_dim] for ki in keys[li]]
            v_h = [vi[hs:hs+head_dim] for vi in values[li]]
            attn_logits = [sum(q_h[j] * k_h[t][j] for j in range(head_dim)) / head_dim**0.5 for t in range(len(k_h))]
            attn_weights = softmax(attn_logits)
            head_out = [sum(attn_weights[t] * v_h[t][j] for t in range(len(v_h))) for j in range(head_dim)]
            x_attn.extend(head_out)
        x = linear(x_attn, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wo'])
        x = [a + b for a, b in zip(x, x_residual)]

        x = rmsnorm(x)
        x = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.mlp_fc1'])
        x = [xi.relu() for xi in x]
        x = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.mlp_fc2'])

v = [0.0] * len(params) # second moment buffer

# Repeat in sequence

for step in range(num_steps):

    doc = docs[step % len(docs)]
    tokens = [BOS] + [uchars.index(ch) for ch in doc] + [BOS]

    # Forward the token sequence through the model, building up the computation graph all the way to the loss.
    keys, values = [[] for _ in range(n_layer)], [[] for _ in range(n_layer)]
    losses = []

        logits = gpt(token_id, pos_id, keys, values)
        probs = softmax(logits)
        loss_t = -probs[target_id].log()
        losses.append(loss_t)
    loss = (1 / n) * sum(losses) # final average loss over the document sequence. May yours be low.

    # Backward the loss, calculating the gradients with respect to all model parameters.
    loss.backward()

the blog post's code blocks, adapted ONLY in configuration to the Fortress v1 nano
setting so the two can be compared:

  vocab 27 (a-z + BOS), n_embd 8, n_head 2, n_layer 1, block_size 8,
  first 2000 non-empty lines of explorations/names.txt in FILE ORDER (no shuffle,
  matching microgpt.fss), 250 steps, Adam(0.01, 0.85, 0.99, 1e-8) + linear decay,
  10 samples at temperature 0.5.

Everything PRNG-touching is Karpathy's own: random.gauss(0, 0.08) for the weights,
random.choices for temperature sampling -- i.e. CPython's Mersenne Twister.
Seed given on the command line.

NOT COMMITTED -- scratchpad only; the blog code's license is unstated.
"""
import math, random, sys

seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 42
names_path = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'names.txt'
random.seed(seed)

# ---------------- dataset (file order; microgpt.fss does not shuffle) ----------
max_docs = 2000
docs = []
with open(names_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        l = line.strip()
        if l:
            docs.append(l)
        if len(docs) >= max_docs:
            break
print(f"num docs: {len(docs)}")

uchars = [chr(97 + i) for i in range(26)]   # microgpt.fss hardcodes a-z
BOS = 26
vocab_size = 27
print(f"vocab size: {vocab_size}")

# ---------------- Value (verbatim from the post) ------------------------------
class Value:
    __slots__ = ('data', 'grad', '_children', '_local_grads')

    def __init__(self, data, children=(), local_grads=()):
        self.data = data
        self.grad = 0
        self._children = children
        self._local_grads = local_grads

    def __add__(self, other):
        other = other if isinstance(other, Value) else Value(other)
        return Value(self.data + other.data, (self, other), (1, 1))

    def __mul__(self, other):
        other = other if isinstance(other, Value) else Value(other)
        return Value(self.data * other.data, (self, other), (other.data, self.data))

    def __pow__(self, other): return Value(self.data**other, (self,), (other * self.data**(other-1),))
    def log(self): return Value(math.log(self.data), (self,), (1/self.data,))
    def exp(self): return Value(math.exp(self.data), (self,), (math.exp(self.data),))
    def relu(self): return Value(max(0, self.data), (self,), (float(self.data > 0),))
    def __neg__(self): return self * -1
    def __radd__(self, other): return self + other
    def __sub__(self, other): return self + (-other)
    def __rsub__(self, other): return other + (-self)
    def __rmul__(self, other): return self * other
    def __truediv__(self, other): return self * other**-1
    def __rtruediv__(self, other): return other * self**-1

    def backward(self):
        topo = []
        visited = set()
        def build_topo(v):
            if v not in visited:
                visited.add(v)
                for child in v._children:
                    build_topo(child)
                topo.append(v)
        build_topo(self)
        self.grad = 1
        for v in reversed(topo):
            for child, local_grad in zip(v._children, v._local_grads):
                child.grad += local_grad * v.grad

# ---------------- model (nano config) -----------------------------------------
n_embd = 8
n_head = 2
n_layer = 1
block_size = 8
head_dim = n_embd // n_head
matrix = lambda nout, nin, std=0.08: [[Value(random.gauss(0, std)) for _ in range(nin)] for _ in range(nout)]
state_dict = {'wte': matrix(vocab_size, n_embd), 'wpe': matrix(block_size, n_embd), 'lm_head': matrix(vocab_size, n_embd)}
for i in range(n_layer):
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wq'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wk'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wv'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.attn_wo'] = matrix(n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.mlp_fc1'] = matrix(4 * n_embd, n_embd)
    state_dict[f'layer{i}.mlp_fc2'] = matrix(n_embd, 4 * n_embd)
params = [p for mat in state_dict.values() for row in mat for p in row]
print(f"num params: {len(params)}")

def linear(x, w):
    return [sum(wi * xi for wi, xi in zip(wo, x)) for wo in w]

def softmax(logits):
    max_val = max(val.data for val in logits)
    exps = [(val - max_val).exp() for val in logits]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [e / total for e in exps]

def rmsnorm(x):
    ms = sum(xi * xi for xi in x) / len(x)
    scale = (ms + 1e-5) ** -0.5
    return [xi * scale for xi in x]

def gpt(token_id, pos_id, keys, values):
    tok_emb = state_dict['wte'][token_id]
    pos_emb = state_dict['wpe'][pos_id]
    x = [t + p for t, p in zip(tok_emb, pos_emb)]
    x = rmsnorm(x)

    for li in range(n_layer):
        x_residual = x
        x = rmsnorm(x)
        q = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wq'])
        k = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wk'])
        v = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wv'])
        keys[li].append(k)
        values[li].append(v)
        x_attn = []
        for h in range(n_head):
            hs = h * head_dim
            q_h = q[hs:hs+head_dim]
            k_h = [ki[hs:hs+head_dim] for ki in keys[li]]
            v_h = [vi[hs:hs+head_dim] for vi in values[li]]
            attn_logits = [sum(q_h[j] * k_h[t][j] for j in range(head_dim)) / head_dim**0.5 for t in range(len(k_h))]
            attn_weights = softmax(attn_logits)
            head_out = [sum(attn_weights[t] * v_h[t][j] for t in range(len(v_h))) for j in range(head_dim)]
            x_attn.extend(head_out)
        x = linear(x_attn, state_dict[f'layer{li}.attn_wo'])
        x = [a + b for a, b in zip(x, x_residual)]
        x_residual = x
        x = rmsnorm(x)
        x = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.mlp_fc1'])
        x = [xi.relu() for xi in x]
        x = linear(x, state_dict[f'layer{li}.mlp_fc2'])
        x = [a + b for a, b in zip(x, x_residual)]

    logits = linear(x, state_dict['lm_head'])
    return logits

# ---------------- Adam --------------------------------------------------------
learning_rate, beta1, beta2, eps_adam = 0.01, 0.85, 0.99, 1e-8
m = [0.0] * len(params)
v = [0.0] * len(params)

num_steps = 250
for step in range(num_steps):
    doc = docs[step % len(docs)]
    tokens = [BOS] + [uchars.index(ch) for ch in doc] + [BOS]
    n = min(block_size, len(tokens) - 1)

    keys, values = [[] for _ in range(n_layer)], [[] for _ in range(n_layer)]
    losses = []
    for pos_id in range(n):
        token_id, target_id = tokens[pos_id], tokens[pos_id + 1]
        logits = gpt(token_id, pos_id, keys, values)
        probs = softmax(logits)
        loss_t = -probs[target_id].log()
        losses.append(loss_t)
    loss = (1 / n) * sum(losses)

    loss.backward()

    lr_t = learning_rate * (1 - step / num_steps)
    for i, p in enumerate(params):
        m[i] = beta1 * m[i] + (1 - beta1) * p.grad
        v[i] = beta2 * v[i] + (1 - beta2) * p.grad ** 2
        m_hat = m[i] / (1 - beta1 ** (step + 1))
        v_hat = v[i] / (1 - beta2 ** (step + 1))
        p.data -= lr_t * m_hat / (v_hat ** 0.5 + eps_adam)
        p.grad = 0

    if (step + 1) % 10 == 0:
        print(f"step {step+1:4d} / {num_steps:4d} | loss {loss.data:.4f}")

# ---------------- inference ---------------------------------------------------
temperature = 0.5
print("--- inference ---")
for sample_idx in range(10):
    keys, values = [[] for _ in range(n_layer)], [[] for _ in range(n_layer)]
    token_id = BOS
    sample = []
    for pos_id in range(block_size):
        logits = gpt(token_id, pos_id, keys, values)
        probs = softmax([l / temperature for l in logits])
        token_id = random.choices(range(vocab_size), weights=[p.data for p in probs])[0]
        if token_id == BOS:
            break
        sample.append(uchars[token_id])
    print(f"sample {sample_idx+1:2d}: {''.join(sample)}")

object MersenneTwister[\N, nat wordsize, nat degree\]
        (seed:Vector[\N,degree\], coeff:N, middle:ZZ32, pivot:ZZ32,
         tampershift0:ZZ32, tampershift1:ZZ32, tampershift2:ZZ32, tampershift3:ZZ32,
         tampermask1:N, tampermask2:N)
    extends SeededRandomGen[\N,N\]

    getter min(): Just[\N\] = just 0
    getter max(): Just[\N\] = just (((1 asif N) LSHIFT wordsize) - 1)
    getter seedSize(): ZZ32 = degree

    var state: Vector[\N,degree\] = refresh(seed)
    var current: ZZ32 = 0

    (** Called once per every `degree` random numbers generated. **)
    private refresh(s:Vector[\N,degree\]): Vector[\N,degree\] = do
        wordmask = ((1 asif N) LSHIFT wordsize) - 1
        lowermask = ((1 asif N) LSHIFT pivot) - 1
        uppermask = wordmask - lowermask
        s': Vector[\N,degree\] := s.copy()
        for i <- seq(0#degree) do
            y: N := (s'[i] BITAND uppermask) BITOR (s'[(i+1) MOD degree] BITAND lowermask)
            x: N := s'[(i+middle) MOD degree] BITXOR (y RSHIFT 1)
            if odd y then x := x BITXOR coeff end
            s'[i] := x BITAND wordmask
        end
        s'
    end
    private refresh(s:Indexed[\N,ZZ32\]): Vector[\N,degree\] =
        refresh(vector[\N,degree\](fn i => seed.get(i)))

    reseed(seedvec:Indexed[\N,ZZ32\]): MersenneTwister[\N,wordsize,degree\] =
        do state := refresh(seedvec); current := 0; self end

    random(): N = do
        if current = degree then
            state := refresh(state)
            current := 0
        end
        y: N := state[current]
        y := y BITXOR (y RSHIFT tampershift0)
        y := y BITXOR ((y LSHIFT tampershift1) BITAND tampermask1)
        y := y BITXOR ((y LSHIFT tampershift2) BITAND tampermask2)
        y := y BITXOR (y RSHIFT tampershift3)
        current += 1
        y
    end

    perturbed(perturbvec:Generator[\ZZ32\]): MersenneTwister[\N,wordsize,degree\] = do
        (*) XXX Not statistically tested!
        perturbgen = MersenneTwisterInit(0)
        perturbvec' = perturbgen.perturbed(perturbvec).randomMany(degree)
        newseed = vector[\ZZ64,degree\](fn i => state[i] BITXOR perturbvec'[i])
        MersenneTwister[\N,wordsize,degree\](newseed, coeff, middle, pivot, tampershift0,
            tampershift1, tampershift2, tampershift3, tampermask1, tampermask2)
    end

"""Compare the two init samplers head to head, at the exact size microgpt uses.

  Fortress path : java.util.Random 48-bit LCG (Math.random) -> Box-Muller, cos
                  branch only, sin partner DISCARDED, u1 clamped at 1e-12.
  CPython path  : MT19937 -> random.gauss, Box-Muller, cos AND sin (pair cached).

java.util.Random is reimplemented exactly (JDK spec: 48-bit LCG,
seed' = (seed*0x5DEECE66D + 0xB) mod 2^48; nextDouble = (next(26)<<27 + next(27))
* 2^-53).
"""
import math, random, statistics as st

MASK = (1 << 48) - 1
MULT = 0x5DEECE66D
ADD = 0xB

class JavaRandom:
    def __init__(self, seed):
        self.seed = (seed ^ MULT) & MASK
    def next(self, bits):
        self.seed = (self.seed * MULT + ADD) & MASK
        return self.seed >> (48 - bits)
    def nextDouble(self):
        return ((self.next(26) << 27) + self.next(27)) * (2.0 ** -53)

def fortress_gauss(rng, std):
    u1 = rng.nextDouble()
    if u1 < 1e-12: u1 = 1e-12
    u2 = rng.nextDouble()
    r = math.sqrt(-2.0 * math.log(u1))
    theta = 2.0 * math.pi * u2
    return std * r * math.cos(theta)

N = 1264          # microgpt nano parameter count
STD = 0.08
TRIALS = 200

def moments(xs):
    m = st.mean(xs); s = st.pstdev(xs)
    z = [(x - m) / s for x in xs]
    sk = sum(v**3 for v in z) / len(z)
    ku = sum(v**4 for v in z) / len(z) - 3.0
    return m, s, sk, ku, max(abs(x) for x in xs) / STD

for name, gen in [
    ('fortress (java LCG + Box-Muller, cos only)',
     lambda s: (lambda r: [fortress_gauss(r, STD) for _ in range(N)])(JavaRandom(s))),
    ('cpython  (MT19937 + random.gauss)',
     lambda s: (lambda r: [r.gauss(0, STD) for _ in range(N)])(random.Random(s))),
]:
    ms, ss, sks, kus, mxs = [], [], [], [], []
    for t in range(TRIALS):
        m, s, sk, ku, mx = moments(gen(1000 + t))
        ms.append(m); ss.append(s); sks.append(sk); kus.append(ku); mxs.append(mx)
    print(f'{name}')
    print(f'  mean   {st.mean(ms):+.6f}  (sd across {TRIALS} draws {st.pstdev(ms):.6f}; theory {STD/math.sqrt(N):.6f})')
    print(f'  stdev  {st.mean(ss):.6f}   (target {STD})')
    print(f'  skew   {st.mean(sks):+.4f}  sd {st.pstdev(sks):.4f}  (theory sd {math.sqrt(6/N):.4f})')
    print(f'  exkurt {st.mean(kus):+.4f}  sd {st.pstdev(kus):.4f}  (theory sd {math.sqrt(24/N):.4f})')
    print(f'  max|z| {st.mean(mxs):.3f} sigma  (range {min(mxs):.3f}..{max(mxs):.3f})')
    print()

# Kolmogorov-Smirnov against the exact normal CDF, pooled 200*1264 draws
def ks(xs):
    xs = sorted(x / STD for x in xs)
    n = len(xs)
    d = 0.0
    for i, x in enumerate(xs):
        F = 0.5 * (1 + math.erf(x / math.sqrt(2)))
        d = max(d, abs(F - i / n), abs((i + 1) / n - F))
    return d, d * math.sqrt(n)

pool_f = []
r = JavaRandom(4242)
for _ in range(TRIALS * N): pool_f.append(fortress_gauss(r, STD))
pool_p = []
rp = random.Random(4242)
for _ in range(TRIALS * N): pool_p.append(rp.gauss(0, STD))
for nm, p in [('fortress', pool_f), ('cpython ', pool_p)]:
    d, stat = ks(p)
    print(f'KS vs N(0,1)  {nm}: D={d:.5f}  D*sqrt(n)={stat:.3f}  (n={len(p)}, 5% crit ~1.358)')

"""Loss-vs-step chart: Fortress native random() runs vs CPython Mersenne-Twister seeds.

Writes prng-chart.svg (standalone, light background, no external assets).
"""
import re, glob, os, statistics as st

S = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
STEPS = list(range(10, 251, 10))

def parse_fs(path):
    d = {}
    for line in open(path):
        m = re.match(r'step (\d+) / \d+\s+loss ([-\d.eE]+)', line)
        if m: d[int(m.group(1))] = float(m.group(2))
    return d

def parse_py(path):
    d = {}
    for line in open(path):
        m = re.match(r'step\s+(\d+) /\s+\d+ \| loss ([\d.]+)', line)
        if m: d[int(m.group(1))] = float(m.group(2))
    return d

fs_v1 = parse_fs(S + '/mg-train.log')
fs_r1 = parse_fs(S + '/fortress_run1.log')
fs_r2 = parse_fs(S + '/fortress_run2.log')

pys = {}
for f in glob.glob(S + '/py_seed*.log'):
    seed = int(re.search(r'seed(\d+)', f).group(1))
    d = parse_py(f)
    if len(d) == 25: pys[seed] = d
seeds = sorted(pys)

band_lo = [min(pys[s][k] for s in seeds) for k in STEPS]
band_hi = [max(pys[s][k] for s in seeds) for k in STEPS]
band_med = [st.median([pys[s][k] for s in seeds]) for k in STEPS]

W, H = 900, 430
L, R, T, B = 58, 150, 22, 46
xmax, ymin, ymax = 250, 1.4, 3.6
def X(s): return L + (W - L - R) * s / xmax
def Y(v): return T + (H - T - B) * (ymax - v) / (ymax - ymin)
def path(pairs): return "M" + " L".join(f"{X(s):.1f} {Y(v):.2f}" for s, v in pairs)
def pts(d): return sorted((k, v) for k, v in d.items())

grid = ''
for gv in [1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5]:
    grid += f'<line x1="{L}" y1="{Y(gv):.1f}" x2="{W-R}" y2="{Y(gv):.1f}" stroke="#dfe3e8" stroke-width="1"/>'
    grid += f'<text x="{L-8}" y="{Y(gv)+4:.1f}" font-size="12" fill="#5c6570" text-anchor="end">{gv:.1f}</text>'
for gs in [0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250]:
    grid += f'<line x1="{X(gs):.1f}" y1="{T}" x2="{X(gs):.1f}" y2="{H-B}" stroke="#eef1f4" stroke-width="1"/>'
    grid += f'<text x="{X(gs):.1f}" y="{H-B+18}" font-size="12" fill="#5c6570" text-anchor="middle">{gs}</text>'

        + " L" + " L".join(f"{X(k):.1f} {Y(v):.2f}" for k, v in zip(reversed(STEPS), reversed(band_lo))) + " Z")

thin = ''.join(f'<path d="{path(pts(pys[s]))}" fill="none" stroke="#8aa4c8" stroke-width="0.8" opacity="0.55"/>'
               for s in seeds)

leg = [
    ('#2f6fb5', 'CPython MT19937', f'{len(seeds)} seeds: band + median'),
    ('#c0392b', 'Fortress run A', 'native random(), v1 log'),
    ('#e07b39', 'Fortress run B', 'native random(), rerun'),
    ('#8d6e63', 'Fortress run C', 'native random(), to step 190'),
]
ly = T + 16
legend = ''
for col, name, sub in leg:
    legend += f'<line x1="{W-R+4}" y1="{ly}" x2="{W-R+26}" y2="{ly}" stroke="{col}" stroke-width="2.4"/>'
    legend += f'<text x="{W-R+32}" y="{ly+4}" font-size="12" fill="#22282e">{name}</text>'
    legend += f'<text x="{W-R+4}" y="{ly+18}" font-size="10.5" fill="#6b7480">{sub}</text>'
    ly += 40

svg = f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" width="{W}" height="{H}" font-family="ui-sans-serif,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">
<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="#ffffff"/>
{grid}
<path d="{band}" fill="#2f6fb5" opacity="0.14"/>
{thin}
<path d="{path(list(zip(STEPS, band_med)))}" fill="none" stroke="#2f6fb5" stroke-width="2.4"/>
<path d="{path(pts(fs_v1))}" fill="none" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2.2"/>
<path d="{path(pts(fs_r1))}" fill="none" stroke="#e07b39" stroke-width="2.2"/>
<path d="{path(pts(fs_r2))}" fill="none" stroke="#8d6e63" stroke-width="2.0" stroke-dasharray="5 3"/>
<line x1="{L}" y1="{H-B}" x2="{W-R}" y2="{H-B}" stroke="#aeb6bf" stroke-width="1"/>
<line x1="{L}" y1="{T}" x2="{L}" y2="{H-B}" stroke="#aeb6bf" stroke-width="1"/>
<text x="{(L+W-R)/2:.0f}" y="{H-8}" font-size="12.5" fill="#3b434c" text-anchor="middle">training step</text>
<text x="16" y="{(T+H-B)/2:.0f}" font-size="12.5" fill="#3b434c" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90 16 {(T+H-B)/2:.0f})">per-document loss</text>
{legend}
</svg>'''
open(S + '/prng-chart.svg', 'w').write(svg)
print(f'wrote prng-chart.svg: {len(seeds)} python seeds, fortress points '
      f'v1={len(fs_v1)} r1={len(fs_r1)} r2={len(fs_r2)}')

# also dump the numbers used
with open(S + '/chart-data.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('step\tFS-v1\tFS-r1\tFS-r2\tpy-min\tpy-med\tpy-max\n')
